continuation.text:
The existing implementation already enforced the "at least one resource left unallocated" rule. After all requests are summed, it returns `True` only if some resource has usage below its capacity. It also returns `False` on over-allocation. I kept that logic. I haven't run the code or written any checks.

I made two small cleanups in `src/solution.py`:
- **Empty resources:** an empty resources dictionary used to raise `ValueError`, which the requirements don't call for. It now returns `False`, since no resource can remain unallocated.
- **Dead code:** I removed unreachable checks, namely the `None` checks that came after the `isinstance` checks and a nested-dict check that could never trigger.

The public signature, validation and over-allocation behaviour are unchanged.

I read "at least one resource" as at least one resource type with spare capacity. Under that reading, a request set that uses all of one type is still valid if another type has spare capacity.
